discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap concept and its realization in light-controlling devices
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently showed that a periodic dielectric can forbid photon propagation in all directions. This photonic band gap lets us control spontaneous emission and localize light, and it ended the assumption that the optical properties of matter are fixed by its atoms. Yablonovitch then made the first three-dimensional photonic band-gap structure. John developed the theory of photon localization and of atom-photon bound states inside the gap. Noda turned the concept into working physics and technology: he made complete-band-gap crystals at optical wavelengths, recorded record-Q nanocavities, and built photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers that give high power in a single mode. Photonic crystals now support nanolasers, slow light, quantum-dot single-photon sources, cavity QED on chips, and topological photonics. Few ideas in modern optics have been as original, fruitful and widely used.
